sentences.text: L Ushanth Kumar vs Apsrtc on 17 October, 2023

The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No.3974 of 2014
Judgment:

Aggrieved by the impugned order dated 29.08.2012 on the file of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal -cum- III Additional District Judge, Tirupati, passed in M.V.O.P.No.117 of 2010, whereby the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim against the respondent, the instant appeal is preferred by the appellant/ claimant for enhancement of claim amount.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal -cum- III Additional District Judge, Tirupati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The claimant filed a Claim Petition under section 166(1)(a) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the respondent praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.6,00,000/- towards compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 17.10.2009.

4. Facts germane to dispose of this appeal, in brief, stated as follows:
2 VGKRJ MACMA 3974 of 2014 On 17.10.2009 at about 6.30 p.m. near Tower Clock Junction of Nagari Municipality, while the petitioner boarded Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) bus bearing No.AP10Z 9316, hereinafter referred to as 'offending vehicle', of Puttur depot to go to his village, the driver of the bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, resulting which the petitioner fell down from the bus and left back wheel of the bus ran over the right foot of the petitioner, as a result, the petitioner sustained serious crush and fracture injuries to his both legs besides other simple injuries all over the body.

entities.text: Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The conductor of the bus did not close the door of the bus after boarding the passengers and not gave proper signals to the driver to stop the bus to avoid accident.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent act of the driver and conductor of the offending vehicle.

5. The respondent filed counter denying the claim of claimant and contended that the claimant is not entitled any compensation and the respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the claimant.
3 VGKRJ MACMA 3974 of 2014 6.

Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
i. Whether the accident occurred due to negligence of the driver of APSRTC bus bearing registration No.AP10Z 9316 and that resulted in causing injuries to the L Ushanth Kumar vs Apsrtc on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154433921/
1 petitioner?
ii.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation and if so, to what amount and payable by whom?
iii. To what relief?
7. During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioner, PW1 to PW5 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A12 were marked.
No oral or documentary evidence was adduced on behalf of respondent.

8. At the culmination of the enquiry, after considering the evidence on record and on appreciation of the same, the Tribunal has given a finding that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle and also the negligence of conductor of offending vehicle and the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.4,86,208/- to the claimant towards total compensation.
Aggrieved by the same, the claimant filed the 4 VGKRJ MACMA 3974 of 2014 present appeal claiming the remaining balance of compensation amount.
9. Heard Sri O.Udaya Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri K.Viswanatham, learned counsel for the respondent.

10. Now, the point for consideration is:
 Whether the Order of Tribunal needs any  interference?
If so to what extent?
11. POINT:-
In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioner relied on the evidence of PW1 to PW5 and Ex.A1 to Ex.A12.
PW1 is none other than the father of the minor petitioner.
As per his evidence, the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, in which the claimant sustained fatal injuries.

On appreciation of the entire evidence on record, the Tribunal arrived to a conclusion that the accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle/APSRTC bus, in which the petitioner sustained bleeding injuries.
I do not find any illegality in the said finding given by the Tribunal.
5 VGKRJ MACMA 3974 of 2014 12.
Coming to the quantum of compensation, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.4,86,208/- to the claimant towards total compensation.

In order to prove the injuries sustained by the claimant,
the petitioner relied on the evidence of PW3- Dr.D.J.Parthiban.

As per the evidence of PW3, who is working as a Consultant Orthopedic Surgeon in a Corporate hospital at Chennai, the petitioner was treated in their hospital from 17.10.2009 to 10.11.2009 and he further deposed that the petitioner sustained three fracture injuries and he also underwent surgery in their hospital and Ex.A9 is the inpatient bill for Rs.2,72,180/-, Ex.A10 is the pharmacy bills and Ex.A5 is the discharge summary L Ushanth Kumar vs Apsrtc on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154433921/
2 issued by their hospital.

PW2, who is working as Billing Section Manager, Soundarapandian Bone and Joint Hospital, Chennai, deposed that the petitioner was treated in their hospital as inpatient for 24 days i.e., from 17.10.2009 to 10.11.2009 and they have collected an amount of Rs.2,72,180/-
from the petitioner towards full and final settlement.

entities.text: Soundarapandian Bone and Joint Hospital, Chennai
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: PW4-T.Dhananjayulu, who is the proprietor of Varasiddi Travels, Nagari, deposed that the father of the minor petitioner engaged his vehicles on 17.10.2009, 10.11.2009, 17.11.2009, 04.12.2009, 08.12.2009 and 24.11.2009 for taking the petitioner to 6 VGKRJ MACMA 3974 of 2014 Soundarapandian Bone and Joint Hospital, Chennai.

entities.text: Soundarapandian Bone and Joint Hospital, Chennai
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: PW5 is the eye-witness to the accident.
As stated supra, the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle-APSRTC bus only.
The evidence of PW5 also supports the case of the claimant.
13. The material on record reveals that the petitioner sustained three grievous injuries.
The Tribunal rightly awarded an amount of Rs.45,000/- towards compensation for pain and suffering.

Since the petitioner sustained severe fatal injuries and he also underwent treatment as inpatient at Corporate hospital, Chennai for a period of one (1) month, the Tribunal by assailing reasons rightly came to conclusion that the petitioner is not able to concentrate on his studies and his educational career is spoiled and on considering the same an amount of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards loss of income.
On considering the evidence of PW3 coupled with Ex.A5 and Ex.A7, the Tribunal rightly came to conclusion that the minor petitioner is suffering with disability of 20%.

The learned counsel for the claimant placed a reliance in the judgment of Supreme Court of India in between Master Ayush Vs.
Insurance Company Limited 7 VGKRJ MACMA 3974 of 2014 and another1.

entities.text:
Master Ayush Vs.
Insurance Company Limited 7 VGKRJ MACMA 3974 of 2014
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On considering the decision of the Apex Court relied by the claim petitioner, who is the appellant herein, the notional income of the petitioner, taken by the Tribunal, for an amount of Rs.15,000/- is enhanced to Rs.18,000/-.
As stated supra, the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner is 20% and the relevant multiplier applicable for the age of petitioner is 15.

Accordingly, an amount of Rs.54,000/-
(18,000 x 20% x 15) is awarded towards 20% disability sustained by the claimant.
On considering the evidence of PW2 and PW3 and on considering the entire material on record, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.2,72,180/- towards inpatient medical bills.
The Tribunal also considered out-patient medical bill for Rs.1,428/- and the same was awarded by the Tribunal on considering Ex.A8.

On considering the Ex.A10 medical bills coupled with the prescriptions prescribed by PW2,
the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.48,000/- towards outpatient medical bills.
On considering the evidence of PW4 coupled with Ex.A10 transport bills, the Tribunal rightly awarded an amount of Rs.14,600/- towards transport expenses.
In total, an amount of Rs.3,36,208/- was awarded towards medical bills and (2022) 7 SCC 738 8 VGKRJ MACMA 3974 of 2014 transport expenses by the tribunal.
I do not find any illegality in awarding an amount of Rs.3,36,208/- towards compensation to the claimant under the above said heads.

Since the petitioner sustained severe injuries and underwent surgeries, an amount of Rs.50,000/- was awarded by the Tribunal towards future expenses with regard to the surgeries to be undergone by the minor petitioner.
I do not find any illegality in awarding the said Rs.50,000/- under the head of future medical expenses awarded by the Tribunal.

The material on record reveals that the petitioner underwent treatment as inpatient for a period of one month, therefore, on considering the entire material on record, I am of considered view that an amount of Rs.10,000/- is to be awarded towards nutrition of food and an amount of Rs.20,000/- is to be awarded towards loss of amenities to the claim petitioner since the petitioner was aged about 8 years.

On considering the entire material on record, I am of considered L Ushanth Kumar vs Apsrtc on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154433921/
3 view that it is desirable to award an amount of Rs.6,000/- towards attendant charges.
In total, the claimant is entitled the compensation amount of Rs.5,31,208/-.
Accordingly, the amount of Rs.4,86,208/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.5,31,208/-.
9 VGKRJ MACMA 3974 of 2014 14.

In the result, this appeal is partly allowed, modifying the order dated 29.08.2012 passed in MVOP No.117/2010 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- III Additional District Judge, Tirupati

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: , consequently the claim amount is enhanced from Rs.4,86,208/- to Rs.5,31,208/-.
The petitioner is entitled the enhanced compensation of Rs.45,000/- with interest @6% p.a. from the date of petition, till the date of realization.
The respondent is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation with interest as ordered above, before the Tribunal within two months from the date of this judgment.
On such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to withdraw the same along with accrued interest thereon.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
V.GOPALA KRISHNA RAO, J Dated: .10.2023.
